name: Checking If Models Understand Across Languages and Time
gist: Papers test whether models work in multiple languages, understand time-series patterns, handle long conversations, and maintain knowledge across different contexts and sequences.
explain: A model trained mostly on English text might be great at English but terrible at Chinese or Arabic. A model trained on text from 2020 might not understand events or slang from 2024. A model tested on single questions might fail when you ask it a series of questions that build on each other—holding context across a long conversation. This subtheme is about building benchmarks that test whether models work across languages, time periods, and long sequences.

The difficulty is that language and knowledge change. The same word means different things in different languages and contexts. Knowledge becomes outdated: facts true in 2020 might be false in 2024. Long conversations are hard because models have finite memory and processing capacity, and they have to track who said what, what was decided, what still matters. Building tests for these challenges means creating benchmarks in many languages, testing on recent events and evolving language use, and creating long-form conversational tasks where context actually matters.

Researchers approach this in several ways. Some build multilingual benchmarks: the same task in many languages to see whether a model works equally well across language families. Others create temporal benchmarks: tests that require knowing when an event happened or what the current date context is. Still others build conversation-based benchmarks where a model has to maintain context over many turns, or time-series benchmarks where a model has to predict or understand sequential patterns. The goal is to measure how well models work across the dimensions that matter most in real-world use: language, time, and long-form reasoning.

papers.title: Mix-Ecom: Towards Mixed-Type E-Commerce Dialogues with Complex Domain Rules
papers.contribution: Reveals that current e-commerce agents lack sufficient capabilities, providing benchmark with diverse dialogue types, tasks, and rules for future evaluation.

papers.title: MultiHal: Multilingual Dataset for Knowledge-Graph Grounded Evaluation of LLM Hallucinations
papers.contribution: Shows 0.12-0.36 point improvement in semantic similarity, 0.16-0.36 in NLI entailment, and 0.29-0.42 in hallucination detection with KG-RAG over vanilla QA across languages.

papers.title: Unpacking Human Preference for LLMs: Demographically Aware Evaluation with the HUMAINE Framework
papers.contribution: Reveals google/gemini-2.5-pro ranks first with 95.6% posterior probability and uncovers significant preference heterogeneity by age with 65% tie rate on abstract dimensions.

papers.title: BEDTime: A Unified Benchmark for Automatically Describing Time Series
papers.contribution: Evaluating 17 state-of-the-art models shows: dedicated time series-language models underperform, vision-language models surprisingly capable, language-only methods worst, and all approaches fragile to real-world robustness tests.

papers.title: BIRD-INTERACT: Re-imagining Text-to-SQL Evaluation via Lens of Dynamic Interactions
papers.contribution: Provides realistic benchmark covering full CRUD spectrum with 600 tasks featuring ambiguous and follow-up sub-tasks requiring dynamic interaction.

papers.title: Beyond Model Ranking: Predictability-Aligned Evaluation for Time Series Forecasting
papers.contribution: SCP aligns with forecasting errors across diverse forecasters; stratified evaluation reveals complementary architectural strengths and time-varying task difficulty.

papers.title: ConTSG-Bench: A Unified Benchmark for Conditional Time Series Generation
papers.contribution: Benchmarks reveal limitations and critical challenges in structural controllability and downstream task utility under complex conditions.

papers.title: Evaluating Language Models in Realistic Conversational Contexts
papers.contribution: Develops Mixture-of-Judges framework improving correlation with human judgment by ~30% over existing automatic metrics and LLM-as-a-judge approaches.

papers.title: Terminal Dimension Reduction for Time Series with Applications
papers.contribution: Provides first dimension-free coresets for time-series clustering with empirical results showing favorable comparison to PCA.

papers.title: TimeLAVA: Learning-Agnostic Valuation for Time Series Data
papers.contribution: Produces significantly more informative value scores than existing methods for anomaly detection, data pruning, and label noise detection across diverse real-world time series datasets.
